caption_L1: Public sector expenditure on unemployment benefits in the United Kingdom (UK) from 2009/10 to 2019/20 (in billion GBP) is a bar graph. Along the y-axis, Year is defined. Expenditure in billion GBP is plotted using a linear scale of range 0 to 6 on the x-axis.
caption_L2L3: The graph shows that the greatest year for public sector expenditure on unemployment benefits in the UK was 2012/13, with nearly 6 billion GBP spent. From this point on, the spending in this area rapidly and consistently decreases, reaching a low in the last year shown (2019/2020) at just over 1 billion GBP. Before 2012/2013, all the years spending accumulate to above 5 billion GBP, but afterwards the spending never goes above 5 billion GBP again.
